miniProject.title: Tokenizer and corpus audit pack
miniProject.brief: Turn a small public-domain corpus into a packed, auditable training split with your own byte-level BPE. Every packed token traces back to a source document, and every claim about the split, such as no duplicates across splits and no planted evaluation text in training, is backed by a test or a report you can rerun.
steps: Start one repository for the whole stage: a uv project with a `src` package and a `tests` folder. Pick a small public-domain corpus under 20 MB, such as a few Project Gutenberg books or the TinyStories validation file.

Implement BPE training, encoding, decoding and streaming encoding. Connect them to `tests/adapters.py` in your clone of the CS336 assignment and pass `tests/test_train_bpe.py` and `tests/test_tokenizer.py`.
Serialize the tokenizer canonically with a content hash, and make loading fail on a changed merge list, special-token set or normalization policy.

Assign raw documents to train and evaluation splits by a stable hash of their raw ID, before fitting the tokenizer or packing. Record source, raw hash, normalized hash and transform version for each document.

Remove exact and near duplicates while keeping cluster lineage, and simulate a hash collision to show that your byte comparison catches it. Plant three evaluation passages in training documents, make your contamination probe find them, and review its false matches.
Apply a reason-coded filter table with quality rules and synthetic PII and toxicity examples, and report document, byte and token yields per source.
Pack the training split with EOS boundaries, a loss mask and per-token document IDs. Write ordered, checksummed shards and a manifest, and show that an interrupted run produces byte-identical shards.

Write tests against small hand-worked examples: the loss mask drops the prediction from one document's EOS to the next document's first token, the document attention mask blocks attention across documents and to future positions, exact deduplication treats NFC-equivalent strings as equal, near-duplicate scores equal exact Jaccard similarity of word-shingle sets, and the 13-gram contamination fraction of a planted passage is what you computed by hand.
deliverables: The tokenizer package with its serialized artifact, identity hash and passing CS336 tokenizer tests.
The packed training split: shards, manifest, per-token document IDs and loss masks.
An audit report: split assignment, duplicate clusters, contamination hits with reviewed false matches, filter yields and per-source token shares.
A resume test that interrupts packing mid-shard and compares checksums with an uninterrupted run.

checks.name: CS336 `tests/test_train_bpe.py` and `tests/test_tokenizer.py`
checks.note: Run in your clone of the assignment with `tests/adapters.py` calling your package. `test_encode_memory_usage` is expected to fail.

rubric.pass: Both CS336 tokenizer test files pass with no unexpected failures.
rubric.strong: Your own property tests also cover every two-chunk split of multilingual strings and partial special-token prefixes, and a reloaded artifact gives identical IDs.

rubric.pass: Loading rejects a changed merge list or special-token set.
rubric.strong: The hash covers a canonical serialization of vocabulary bytes, merges, special tokens, regex and normalization policy, and the error names what changed.

rubric.pass: Splits are assigned before tokenizer fitting and packing, and every packed token maps to a document ID.
rubric.strong: Duplicate clusters that span splits are quarantined or reassigned, and the report counts them.

rubric.pass: Your mask tests pass on a hand-worked sequence that packs at least two documents.
rubric.strong: You explain which predictions the attention mask alone would not remove, and a deliberately wrong mask makes your tests fail.

rubric.pass: The probe finds every planted passage and the report lists its hits.
rubric.strong: The report reviews false matches, states what the probe cannot detect, such as paraphrase or translation, and simulates a hash collision.

rubric.pass: Rerunning the pipeline gives the same manifest checksums.
rubric.strong: An interrupted run resumed from its saved cursor, RNG and partial pack gives byte-identical shards, and a changed config is rejected on resume.

miniProject.feedsInto: Capstone artifact 1, the tokenizer and corpus audit pack. Sections 3 and 4 train and evaluate on this split, and every token count in the capstone uses this tokenizer.
